mainTopic: Excluding a טריפה from the ark; how to count the three days before the gentiles' holidays; the reason for the ban on doing business with them
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of how a טריפה is kept out of נח's ark, according to the view that a טריפה can give birth. For that view the גמרא learns it from the word 'אתך' ('with you'): the animals had to be like נח. It then shows that נח himself was whole, because otherwise הקב"ה would have told him to bring only defective animals. The words 'לחיות זרע' still teach that the animals had to be able to reproduce, which rules out old or castrated ones. Next the גמרא asks whether the משנה's 'three days' before the gentiles' holidays include the holiday itself. Proofs from רבי ישמעאל, שמואל and רבינא are pushed off or limited. רב אשי's proof from the word 'before' in the משנה is accepted: the three days do not include the holiday. Finally the גמרא asks whether the ban exists because of the gentile's profit or because of לפני עור. It begins to challenge the practical difference using a ברייתא of רבי נתן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What about the view that a טריפה can give birth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from 'לחיות זרע' according to the opinion that a טריפה can give birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says a טריפה can give birth, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a gap in the earlier proof. If a טריפה can have babies, the words 'to keep seed alive' don't exclude it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof assumed that a טריפה cannot reproduce, so it was not 'seed' to keep alive. The opinion that a טריפה יולדת removes that assumption. Now we need a new source to keep a טריפה out of the ark.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect
According to the one who says
What can be said? A question asking how this view handles the issue

phrases.english: But according to the one who says:
A טריפה gives birth, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵיפָה יוֹלֶדֶת מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'לחיות זרע' that a טריפה was excluded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof only works if a טריפה cannot reproduce. The other view says it can, so the proof fails for that view.

steps.title: The word 'with you' means animals like נח
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אתך' teaches that the animals had to be similar to נח, so a טריפה is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'with you,' meaning animals that are similar to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source. 'With you' means the animals had to resemble נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source does not depend on whether a טריפה can give birth. If the animals must be like נח, and נח was whole, then a defective animal is not like him.

phrases.english: The verse said: 'with you'
with those that are similar to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge with a different verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For the view that a טריפה can give birth, 'לחיות זרע' does not exclude a טריפה, so without another source there would be no way to keep it out of the ark
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אתך' requires animals similar to נח, so a טריפה is excluded

steps.title: Maybe נח himself was a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether נח himself might have been a טריפה, which would make the comparison useless.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps נח himself was a טריפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new proof. If נח was a טריפה, then 'similar to you' would not exclude a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from 'אתך' only works if נח was physically whole. Here the גמרא questions that hidden assumption.

phrases.english: But perhaps נח himself was a טריפה?

steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that נח was whole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If נח was a טריפה, animals 'like him' could include a טריפה.

steps.title: נח is called 'complete'
steps.stepSummary: The verse calls נח 'תמים', which shows he was physically whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Complete' is written about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תורה calls נח 'תמים', meaning whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads 'תמים' as describing נח's body. A whole body means he was not a טריפה.

phrases.english: 'Complete' is written about him.

steps.title: Maybe 'complete' describes his ways
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps 'תמים' describes נח's behavior, not his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he was complete in his ways?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. 'Complete' might be praise for his behavior, not a statement about his body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'תמים' is about character, it tells us nothing about whether נח was a טריפה. That would put the proof from 'אתך' back in doubt.

phrases.english: But perhaps he was 'complete in his ways'?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could mean moral perfection instead.

steps.title: 'Righteous' already covers his ways
steps.stepSummary: The verse already calls נח 'צדיק', so 'תמים' must add something physical.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Righteous' is written about him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that נח's good conduct is already covered by the word 'צדיק'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'צדיק' already describes his good behavior, then 'תמים' should teach something new. That new point is that his body was whole.

phrases.english: 'Righteous' is written about him!
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, בראשית 6:9. 'Righteous' already praises his behavior.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Avoiding a repeated word in the verse

steps.title: Maybe the two words describe two kinds of goodness
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps 'תמים' is about his manner and 'צדיק' is about his deeds, so both words are still about character.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he was 'complete' in his ways and 'righteous' in his deeds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that each word describes a different kind of good character. Then neither word is about his body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes away the argument from repetition, because the two words no longer overlap. So the verse may still not prove that נח was physically whole.

phrases.english: Perhaps 'complete' in his ways,
and 'righteous' in his deeds he was?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא תָּמִים בִּדְרָכָיו צַדִּיק בְּמַעֲשָׂיו הֲוָה
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument that 'תמים' must be physical because 'צדיק' covers behavior
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two words could describe two different parts of character, so neither one is extra.

steps.title: Logic proves נח was whole
steps.stepSummary: If נח were a טריפה, would הקב"ה tell him to bring defective animals like himself and not whole ones? That makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot think נח was a טריפה. If you did, would the Merciful One have told him: bring in ones like you, but don't bring in whole ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the verse-reading approach and answers with plain logic. Telling נח to save only defective animals would be absurd.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If נח were a טריפה, 'animals like you' would mean that only animals with a fatal defect may enter the ark and whole, healthy ones must stay out. No one could think הקב"ה commanded that. So נח must have been whole, and 'אתך' does exclude a טריפה.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא proves that נח was physically whole by logic, not by the wording of the verse. So 'אתך' (animals like נח) excludes a טריפה even for the view that a טריפה can give birth.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind
that נח himself was a טריפה,
for if it would enter your mind
that נח was a טריפה,
would the Merciful One have said to him:
Bring in ones like you,
phrases.notes: He means defective animals, like נח would be if he were a טריפה.

phrases.english: but whole ones do not bring in?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּנֹחַ גּוּפֵיהּ טְרֵיפָה הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the last challenge with logic instead of the wording of the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נח might have been a טריפה, which would make 'אתך' useless
steps.terutzMaskana: נח was certainly whole, so 'אתך' excludes a טריפה

steps.title: Why do we still need 'to keep seed alive'?
steps.stepSummary: Since 'אתך' already excludes a טריפה, what do the words 'לחיות זרע' add?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that he learns it from 'with you,' why do I need 'to keep seed alive'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what job the words 'לחיות זרע' still do, now that 'אתך' handles the טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For this view, 'אתך' does the work of excluding a טריפה. So 'לחיות זרע' looks extra and must be teaching something else.

phrases.english: And now that he derives it from 'with you,'
why do I need 'to keep seed alive'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵאִתָּךְ לְחַיּוֹת זֶרַע לְמָה לִי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'לחיות זרע' teaches for the view that a טריפה can give birth

steps.title: 'Seed' excludes animals that cannot have offspring
steps.stepSummary: From 'אתך' alone, we might think the animals were only for company, so even old or castrated ones could come. 'זרע' teaches that they must be able to reproduce.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had 'with you,' I would have said it was just for company, so even an old one or a castrated one could come. So the Merciful One wrote 'seed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'seed' adds a second requirement: the animals must be able to have offspring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אתך' could sound like the animals were simply there to keep נח company. Then any healthy animal would do, even one that cannot reproduce. The word 'זרע' shows the goal was to continue the species, which rules out old and castrated animals.
steps.whatToRemember: Two words, two jobs: 'אתך' excludes a טריפה (they must be like נח), and 'זרע' excludes animals that cannot reproduce, like old or castrated ones.

phrases.english: If from 'with you,' I would have said
merely for company,
and even an old one and even a castrated one,
so the Merciful One wrote 'seed.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מֵאִתָּךְ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לְצַוְותָּא בְּעָלְמָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'זרע' teaches that only animals able to reproduce were brought, which excludes old and castrated ones
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the view that a טריפה gives birth, 'אתך' excludes a טריפה and 'זרע' excludes animals unable to reproduce.

steps.title: Does the holiday count as one of the three days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה's 'three days' include the holiday day itself, or are three full days before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: the 'three days' in the משנה, do they mean the days before plus the holiday itself, or three days before the holiday, not counting it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about how to count the three forbidden days in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: two days before plus the holiday make three. Option two: three whole days before the holiday, and the holiday is extra. The difference is whether the איסור starts two days early or three days early.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the חכמים)
The days alone, without the holiday

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
"Three days":
Is it them and their holiday,
or perhaps them without their holiday?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, returning to the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the holiday day itself is counted as one of the three forbidden days.

steps.title: Proof from רבי ישמעאל's three days before and after
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל forbids three days before and three after. If the holiday were counted in the three, it would be counted twice, so it must not be counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: רבי ישמעאל says three days before and three days after are forbidden. If you think the three days include the holiday, would רבי ישמעאל count the holiday day both at the start and at the end?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from רבי ישמעאל's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל uses the same phrase, 'three days', both before and after. If the holiday were counted inside the three, it would be counted twice, once in each group. That seems odd, so the three days must be without the holiday.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you think)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yishmael says:
Three days before them and three days after them are forbidden.
If you think it means them and their holiday,
would Rabbi Yishmael take the day of their holiday
and count it at the beginning
and count it again at the end?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That the three days do not include the holiday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ישמעאל's phrase 'three before and three after', which would count the holiday twice otherwise.

steps.title: He said 'three after' only to match 'three before'
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: רבי ישמעאל may count the holiday only in the 'before' group, and just said 'three after' to keep the wording the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he taught 'three before', he also taught 'three after'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the holiday is counted only in the first three days. Really, only two days after are forbidden. רבי ישמעאל just said 'three after' so the wording would match 'three before', so we cannot prove anything from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because of (one thing, the other was also said)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying there really are three days after. It means the 'after' number is just copied for matching wording; really it could be only two.

phrases.english: Since he taught "three before them,"
he also taught "three after them."

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. The question of step 11 is not yet settled here; it is finally resolved by רב אשי's proof in steps 18–20.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the 'after' number is exact, but it may only be said to match the 'before' wording.

steps.title: Proof from שמואל: with נוצרים it is always forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that according to רבי ישמעאל, business with נוצרים is always forbidden. That only works if the three days do not include the holiday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: רב תחליפא בר אבדימי said in the name of שמואל: with נוצרים, according to רבי ישמעאל, it is always forbidden. If you think it means them and their holiday, there are still Wednesday and Thursday that are allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second try to answer the question, from a statement of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holiday of נוצרים is every Sunday. Three days before plus three after plus Sunday covers the whole week, so 'always forbidden' fits. If the holiday were counted inside the three, only two days on each side would be forbidden, leaving Wednesday and Thursday free, and שמואל could not say 'always'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a weekly holiday turns the three-day rule into a question about the whole week.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אַבְדִּימִי
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Tachlifa bar Avdimi said
that Shmuel said:
With Christians, according to Rabbi Yishmael,
phrases.notes: Their holiday is every Sunday, so the forbidden days come around every week.

phrases.english: it is always forbidden.
And if you think it means "them and their holiday,"
there are still the fourth and fifth days that are permitted!
phrases.notes: The fourth and fifth days of the week, meaning Wednesday and Thursday.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אַבְדִּימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a new proof for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That the three days do not include the holiday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's statement that business with נוצרים is always forbidden according to רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: The question was only about the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The questioner says he never had a doubt about רבי ישמעאל. His question is about the view of the רבנן, so שמואל's proof does not answer it.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי ישמעאל I never had a question. Clearly it means three days without the holiday. My question is according to the רבנן: what do they hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from שמואל by narrowing the question. The doubt was only about how the רבנן count the three days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's statement proves that רבי ישמעאל does not count the holiday in the three days. But the רבנן disagree with רבי ישמעאל, so their view could be different. The question is now reopened, but only for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no question about it
the days themselves, without their holiday

steps.confusionAlert: Step 14's proof was not wrong. It just only works for רבי ישמעאל. The question that remains is only about the רבנן, and steps 16–20 deal with it.

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לָא קָמִבַּעְיָא לִי,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yishmael, I have no question,
because it is them without their holiday,
phrases.notes: In other words, the three days are counted without the holiday day itself.

phrases.english: where I do have a question
is according to the Rabbis: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אליבא דרבי ישמעאל לא קמבעיא לי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 14's proof to רבי ישמעאל and reopens the question for the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial. The proof stands for רבי ישמעאל but says nothing about the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof was built on רבי ישמעאל's view, and the question was really about the רבנן.

steps.title: רבינא's proof from the eight-day holiday of קלנדא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא cites the משנה's list of holidays and רב חנין בר רבא's explanation that קלנדא lasts eight days. If the three days included the holiday, the restricted period would be ten days, not three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Come and hear. The משנה lists the gentile holidays: קלנדא, סטרונייא, and קרטסים. רב חנין בר רבא explained that קלנדא is the eight days after the winter solstice, and סטרונייא is the eight days before it. A memory sign is the פסוק 'behind and before You have hemmed me in.' Now, if the three days include the holiday, it would add up to ten days!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a proof for the view of the רבנן. He first sets up the facts about the holidays, then points out a math problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קלנדא lasts eight days. If the holiday were counted inside the 'three days,' you would get two days before plus eight holiday days, which is ten. The משנה would then not call it 'three days.' So it seems the three days are all before the holiday.

keyTerms.meaning: A Roman holiday after the winter solstice
A Roman holiday before the winter solstice
the turning point of the season (here, the winter solstice)

phrases.english: Ravina said: Come and hear,
"And these are the holidays of the gentiles:
phrases.notes: This is a quote from a later משנה in the פרק.

phrases.english: Kalenda, Saturnalia, and Kratesis."
And Rav Chanin bar Rava said:
Kalenda is the eight days after the winter solstice,
Saturnalia is the eight days before the winter solstice,
and your memory sign is: "Behind and before You have hemmed me in."
phrases.notes: תהלים 139:5. 'Behind' (after) comes first, just like קלנדא, the holiday after the solstice, is listed first.

phrases.english: And if you think it means them together with their holiday,
then there are ten days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question that step 15 reopened for the רבנן; the proof is rejected in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The three days do not include the holiday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing the holidays, with רב חנין בר רבא's explanation that קלנדא lasts eight days.

steps.title: All of קלנדא counts as one day
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The תנא treats all eight days of קלנדא as a single holiday day, so the count still comes to three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא counts all of קלנדא as one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבינא's proof by changing how the holiday is counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten-day problem only works if each day of קלנדא counts on its own. If the whole holiday counts as one 'day,' then two days before plus the holiday is three. So the three days could still include the holiday.

phrases.english: The Tanna counts all of Kalenda
as one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנא כוליה קלנדא חד יומא הוא חשיב ליה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed each day of קלנדא is counted separately.

steps.title: רב אשי's proof from the wording 'before their holidays'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points to the משנה's wording, 'before the holidays of the gentiles, three days.' If the holiday were included, the משנה should have just said 'the holidays of the gentiles, three days.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Come and hear. The משנה says 'before the holidays of the gentiles, three days.' If you think it includes the holiday itself, the משנה should have said 'the holidays of the gentiles, three days'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a new proof from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'before' (לפני) suggests that all three days come before the holiday. If the holiday day were one of the three, the word 'before' would not fit. The משנה would have said simply 'their holidays, three days.'

keyTerms.meaning: let it teach: it should have said

steps.whatToRemember: This round has two proofs about the רבנן. רבינא's proof from the eight days of קלנדא was pushed off. רב אשי's proof rests on the word 'before' in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Come and hear:
"Before the holidays of the gentiles, three days,"
and if you think it means them together with their holiday,
let it teach: "The holidays of the gentiles, three days"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבינא's proof is rejected, רב אשי offers a new proof based on wording.
steps.raayaObject: The three days do not include the holiday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'before' (לפני) in the משנה's opening phrase.

steps.title: Blocking a way out of רב אשי's proof
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say the word 'before' only rules out the days after the holiday. The גמרא answers that if so, the משנה should have worded it differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the word 'before their holidays' is there to rule out the days after the holiday, then the משנה should have said: 'the holidays of the gentiles, three days before them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still building רב אשי's proof from the wording of the משנה. It shuts down a possible escape before anyone can use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could argue that 'before' does not show the holiday is excluded. It might only show that the forbidden days come before the holiday and not after it. The גמרא says that if that were the point, the משנה had a clearer way to say it: name the holidays first and then add 'three days before them.'

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a possible objection
Let it teach, meaning the text should have said

phrases.english: And if you would say:
That which it teaches, 'before their holidays'
is to exclude the days after their holidays,
then let it teach: 'The holidays of gentiles,
three days before them!'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, הַאי דְּקָתָנֵי לִפְנֵי אֵידֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רב אשי's proof by heading off a possible deflection.
steps.raayaObject: That the three days do not include the holiday
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the words in the משנה

steps.title: Conclusion: the three days do not include the holiday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the three days are counted without the holiday itself, and it accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the three days are apart from their holidays. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's proof. The three forbidden days come before the holiday and do not include it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier proofs were pushed away, but this one, based on the משנה's wording, holds up. The double 'שמע מינה' shows the גמרא fully agrees, and this question is now settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: a conclusion is drawn and then confirmed

steps.whatToRemember: The three days in the משנה are three full days before the holiday. The holiday day itself is not one of the three.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:
they are three days without their holidays.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from רב אשי's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three days before the gentiles' holidays do not include the holiday itself.

steps.title: Why is business before their holiday forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: is the ban because the gentile's profit leads him to thank his idol, or because of the איסור of לפני עור?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: is it because of the profit, or maybe because of 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic and asks for the reason behind the ban in the משנה. It gives two possible reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: the gentile makes money, feels happy, and thanks his idol on the holiday. Reason two: helping him get what he needs for idol worship is causing someone to sin, which is לפני עור. The reason matters because each one forbids different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them: a question raised in the בית המדרש
Do not put a stumbling block before the blind: the איסור against helping someone sin

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
Is it because of the profit,
or perhaps because of
'And before the blind do not put a stumbling block'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the reason for the משנה's ban.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ban is because of the gentile's profit or because of לפני עור

steps.title: The practical difference: a gentile who already owns an animal
steps.stepSummary: The two reasons give different results when the gentile already has his own animal. The profit reason still forbids the sale. The לפני עור reason would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference? When he has his own animal. If you say it is because of profit, he is still making a profit. If you say it is because of לפני עור, he already has his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question matters by giving a case where the two reasons lead to different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the gentile already owns an animal for his offering, selling him another still gives him profit, so the profit reason still forbids it. But he does not need the Jew in order to sin, so the sale seems not to be a 'stumbling block' and לפני עור would allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: He has one of his own

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
Where he has an animal of his own.
If you say it is because of profit,
here too he gives him profit, so it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ מִשּׁוּם ״עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל״ —
phrases.english: If you say it is because of 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind,'
he already has his own animal, so the sale does not help him sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical difference between the two reasons asked about in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the gentile already owns an animal: the profit reason forbids the sale, while the לפני עור reason would allow it.

steps.title: Does owning an animal really avoid לפני עור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the claim that there is no לפני עור when the gentile already has his own animal, and begins quoting a ברייתא from רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he has his own, does one not violate 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind'? But it was taught: רבי נתן said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the practical difference it just gave. It is setting up a ברייתא from רבי נתן, which will be quoted next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 assumed that helping a person who could sin without you is not לפני עור. The גמרא now doubts this and is about to bring רבי נתן's ברייתא to show that you can still be guilty.

phrases.english: And if he already has his own,

phrases.aramaic: לָא עָבַר מִשּׁוּם ״עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל״?
phrases.english: does one not violate 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind'?
But was it not taught: רבי נתן said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אִית לֵיהּ לָא עָבַר מִשּׁוּם עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption behind the practical difference in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that לפני עור does not apply when the gentile already owns an animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא from רבי נתן will be brought to suggest that לפני עור can apply even when the sinner could manage without your help.
